entries.title: Becoming a citizen
q: how do i become a citizen
how to join the village as a citizen
what does being a citizen do
become a resident of the town
entries.answer: Once the town counts you a friend, ask any folk 'Live here?' (Town, then Council). It costs 20 coins, or nothing if the town built you a house.
more: It's free if the town already built you a house; otherwise 20 coins to the treasury, and its builders put up a house for you on one of its lots.
steps: Be a Friend of the village (see Making friends).
Talk → Town → Council → Live here? (or U → Become a citizen).
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → Live here?
tips: Citizens vote on the council, get a tenth off at the shop and café, take from the stores without it being theft, and may stand for leader.
'Citizen of <town>' shows in gold after your name.
Not a friend yet? The U page says how warm the town is to you, as a number (a friend at 12), under You and the town.
warn: 'We hardly know you yet' means you're not a friend yet; 'Not while you owe the village a fine' means pay up first.

entries.title: The council
q: how do i vote in my town
entries.answer: The council (the elder, the four most-liked folk, and citizens) decides what the town builds next and its taxes. Ask any folk 'The council'.
more: It decides which extra goes up first (café, tavern, smithy, shop, brewery, library) and, at its weekly meeting, the taxes.
steps: Talk → Town → Council → The council: who sits and what it decided.
Sway it: 'You should build a tavern' (Suggest a build…) or 'The taxes should be lower'.
As a citizen, your vote goes to what you proposed.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → The council
tips: Councillors who like you vote your way, more the better they like you.

entries.title: Elections
q: how do i win an election
entries.answer: The town elects its leader every ten days: candidates stand two days before, and every grown folk votes at the board.
more: Two days before, the folk it thinks most of stand (and players may), each promising what it cares about.
The winner's mandate steers the town until the next election.
tips: A Provider fills the larder, a Homemaker builds houses sooner, a Visionary digs, a Guardian mans the walls, a Merchant pays better.
Folk will tell you whether the leader kept its word.

entries.title: Standing for leader (becoming mayor)
q: how to become the leader of a town
can i be the village leader
how do i win an election
can i be boss of the town
can i be in charge of the town
entries.answer: Become a citizen and a friend of the town, then ask any folk 'Stand for leader' (Town, then Council). Win the vote and you lead it.
more: Make up to three promises from what the town wants, ask folk 'Vote for me?', make a speech at the board once a day, and give presents.
Win the count and you lead the town from the Leader's page.
steps: Talk → Town → Council → Stand for leader: the hustings page opens.
Pick up to three promises (lower the tithe, better wages, more guards, a building within N days...).
Canvass: 'Vote for me?' to each folk (once a campaign); 'Make a speech' at the board daily.
Wait for the count at dusk on election day.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → Stand for leader · Vote for me?
Hustings page → promises · Make a speech
warn: Bribes can sway a vote but are an offence if seen, and a scandal turns every voter from you.
In office, broken promises lower your approval; under 30% the town calls a recall.

entries.title: Leading the town (the Leader's page)
q: i won the election now what
what powers does the mayor have
entries.answer: The leader sets the town's plan, its next building, the tithe and wages from the Leader's page. Ask any folk for the Leader's page.
more: As leader you set the town's direction from the Leader's page (Town → Council → Leader's page): the plan (food first, growth, defence, trade, steady, or left to the steward), the next building, the tithe (none to one coin in five), the wages (85 to 120 in the hundred), answers to envoys, and referendums.
The folk still run their days; your steward stands in when you're away.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → Leader's page
tips: Kept promises raise your approval; approval drifts toward how content the town is and slips if you're never seen.
warn: In a famine the steward calls the town to the fields whatever the plan.

entries.title: Referendums and great works
q: how do i vote on a great work
entries.answer: The town votes on its great works, such as a stone bridge, aqueduct, harbour or great road. The board shows each proposal.
more: The leader puts one to the vote two days ahead; the board shows its cost, labour and benefit; if it carries, the whole town builds it.
steps: Watch the board for a proposal.
Folk vote; you can vote in talk, and a player leader can call a referendum from the Leader's page.
tips: A town needs eight grown folk and the Stone Age; an aqueduct, harbour and great road need the Iron Age.
Nothing anybody built is knocked down for a work.

entries.title: Laws, fines, trials and banishment
q: how do i pay a fine
can i steal from the village
what happens if i break buildings
is it a crime to take from chests
entries.answer: Taking from the town's stores (unless you're a citizen) or breaking what it built is against the law. Pay fines with any folk's 'Pay a fine'.
more: First a fine (twice the worth taken, five coins for damage), then a trial before the council (three times the fine), then banishment for seven days.
steps: Pay what you owe: any folk → Town → The watch → Pay a fine.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → The watch → Pay a fine
tips: Ground, trees and crops are anybody's to dig, cut and pick.
warn: Banished, you lose your citizenship, nobody serves you at the counters and the guards turn you out on sight. Outlawed (very serious crimes), a WANTED poster goes up.

entries.title: Taxes
q: do i have to pay taxes
entries.answer: Taxes are set by the council each week; citizens owe the head tax. Pay with any folk's 'Pay my taxes' (Town, then Council).
more: A town levies up to four taxes, set by the council's weekly vote: the head tax (0-3 coins a working hand each tax day), the share of wages (the tithe), the market toll (on sales at the auction or a player's stall) and the war levy (only at war).
steps: Ask 'The taxes' (Town → Council) to hear the rates.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → The taxes · Pay my taxes · Urge lower taxes
warn: Three weeks unpaid and the town thinks less of you. Taxes too high anger the town: grumbling, protests, even a revolt.

entries.title: Knighthood, manors and a retinue
q: how do i become a knight
entries.answer: Serve a town (quests, battles, gifts, taxes, days as a citizen) to 100 points and the council knights you. The Knights page shows your total.
more: Service to a town counts toward a knighthood: quests (12 each), campaigns in its army (20), gifts its folk were glad of, each day as a citizen in good standing, and taxes paid.
At 100, as a citizen and friend with fines paid, the council chooses you and you're dubbed at the hall at dusk (kneel by sneaking).
You get the title, a banner, land with a manor, a retinue from the watch and a council seat.
steps: Watch your service on the Knights page (town's books → Civic).
Come to the hall at dusk when told.
After: 'Retinue, to me!' or 'Retinue, stand down' (Town → Council), and vote on taxes from the Knights page.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Town → Council → My service · Retinue, to me!
warn: Offences take 25 off; a missed muster 30. Two musters missed, or four weeks' knight's fee unpaid, and the title goes.

entries.title: A town's character and identity
entries.answer: Each town has its own character, shaped by its land, its founders and its leaders. Ask any folk 'Town's ways'.
more: Each town leans along seven axes (mercantile/self-sufficient, martial/peaceable, devout/worldly, learned/practical and more), set by its land and founders and drifting with its leaders and what happens to it.
Each leaning does something real: a second market day, more guards, the chapel or tavern sooner, quicker trades.

entries.title: Having your say: petitions to the elder
q: can i tell the elder what to do
entries.answer: Tell the elder what it should order ('we need more miners'): if it thinks well of you, it agrees. One petition per town a day.
more: If it thinks well of you, or you're a citizen in good standing, it agrees, as long as the town can carry it out.
warn: An outcast is not listened to.

entries.title: The town's day: assembly, meetings and the gazette
entries.answer: Each dawn the folk gather briefly at the board for the morning assembly, then go straight to work. The day's news is on the board.
more: The morning assembly is short: at most five lines, about a quarter of a minute, then everybody goes straight to work; the rest of the news goes on the board.
The council meets weekly on taxes and building. The crier calls the news and the gazette sums up the day; the morning news can come to your chat too.
controls: [U] → Everything you can do → Home → The morning news

entries.title: Regalia: crowns and chains of office
q: why is the leader wearing a crown
entries.answer: The town's ruler wears its regalia: a crown and robes, with chains of office for the council.
more: The town's ruler looks the part: crowned and robed in the street, its council and household in chains of office, circlets and plumes.
The Leader page names who wears what.
